summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person is Bethany Anne, Co-Founder and CEO of The Luxora Collective, a business consulting and marketing firm focused on med spas and aesthetic clinics. Throughout this conversation, she worked with Claude to build a series of professional discovery call scripts as formatted Word documents (.docx), all branded for The Luxora Collective with a rose, gold, and charcoal color palette. The primary deliverable was a Growth Engine Discovery Call Script incorporating a live Revenue Leak Scan tool (revleak.theluxoracollective.co), along with a separate Confidential Experience Assessment (secret shopper) discovery call script. An earlier version of a script for a specific prospect (IntegraLife Spa, Fort Myers, FL, owned by Susan Bell) was also produced at the start of the conversation.

Bethany has a clearly defined sales methodology she calls the "feminine approach" or "feminine funnel framework," which prioritizes trust-building, emotional mirroring, slow pacing, permission-based transitions, and identity-painting before any pitch. This framework is central to all scripts and must be preserved in every version. Key elements include: opening with safety and disarming language, one emotional question at a time with explicit pause cues, mirroring the prospect's exact words back verbatim, asking permission before pitching, and a soft two-option close with no fake urgency. Bethany explicitly flagged when versions lost this voice and requested it be restored. She also self-assessed versions critically, asking Claude to rate scripts 1-10 and rebuild to a 9, which Claude did twice with detailed reasoning for each rating and specific improvements made.

Several important content corrections were made during the conversation: financing options are Klarna and Affirm (not CareCredit or Cherry); the delivery description "not homework" was flagged as inaccurate since clients do implement with their own staff, and was rewritten to honestly describe a collaborative build process; a tie-back paragraph claiming "we are not adding anything new" was flagged as incorrect since Luxora does add new structures, and was rewritten to position leak recovery as the floor and new builds as compounding upside. The checkout URL go.theluxoracollective.co/the-luxora-growth-engine was added with explicit instruction to walk clients through it live on the call rather than sending the link alone. The Revenue Leak Scan section was restructured after Bethany clarified the tool collects all four inputs first and only generates results at the end, meaning all commentary must happen after results load, not between inputs. Page breaks were removed throughout so the script reads as one continuous flow. The final Growth Engine script runs six phases with time budgets totaling 45-60 minutes: Open (5 min), Emotional Deep Dive (8 min), Revenue Leak Scan (20 min), Mirror and Reframe (5 min), Pitch (8 min), and Price and Close (7 min).

Call Preparation Sheet
IntegraLife Spa


THE BASICS

Business:  Medical spa and clinical skincare practice
Owner / Spa Director:  Susan Bell
Location:  8660 College Pkwy, Suite 100, Fort Myers, FL 33919 (The Terraces complex, near Cape Coral)
Locations:  1 location - single flagship medical spa

Category:  Medical Spa / Clinical Skincare / Aesthetic Treatments

Financing:  CareCredit and Cherry Financing accepted


ABOUT THE OWNER

Susan Bell is the owner and Spa Director of IntegraLife Spa, with a career spanning the entire beauty and wellness industry - from salon management and sales representation to day spa supervision. She joined what was then Rager Clinical Skin Care over 13 years ago as a manager, eventually purchasing the business and rebranding it as IntegraLife Spa. A self-described product junkie, Susan spends her time researching treatments, ingredients, and innovations to ensure her spa stays ahead of the curve. SOCIAL MEDIA AND DIGITAL PRESENCE

Website

SERVICES

Clinical Facials - customized, results-driven facial treatments for all skin types and concerns
RF Microneedling - radiofrequency microneedling for skin tightening, texture, and anti-aging

Service Enhancements - add-on treatments including lash tinting, dermaplaning, waxing
Integraderm - proprietary skincare product line developed and sold exclusively through the spa
Revision SkinCare and SkinCeuticals retail product lines
Designer Inspired Jewelry - retail offering available in-spa
Gift Cards available for purchase online

WHAT THEY ARE KNOWN FOR

One of the longest-running med spas in Southwest Florida - in business since 1996 (formerly Rager Clinical Skin Care), giving them nearly 30 years of trust and client loyalty in the Fort Myers market
Results-driven, clinical approach to skincare - not a pampering-only spa, but a transformative one. Clients come for measurable skin improvement, not just relaxation
Susan Bell personally built the business from manager to owner - deep practitioner knowledge and hands-on involvement that clients notice and appreciate
Affiliated with Dr. John Nassif, MD, a facial plastic surgeon recognized among America's Top Doctors since 2007 - lending clinical credibility that most day spas cannot offer
Proprietary skincare line (Integraderm) - available only through IntegraLife Spa, creating exclusivity and a reason for clients to stay loyal
Multi-service model covering facials, injectables, laser, body contouring, and retail - a one-stop destination for comprehensive aesthetic care
Exceptionally loyal long-term clientele - reviews frequently mention clients who have been coming for 5, 10, even 15+ years
Located in The Terraces complex on College Pkwy - accessible from both Fort Myers and Cape Coral, serving the broader Southwest Florida market

YOUR ANGLE FOR THIS CALL
DIGITAL AND VISIBILITY GAPS
IntegraLife Spa has been in business for nearly 30 years but their digital presence looks like it has not been touched in years. Instagram has only 314 followers, there is no TikTok, no paid ad infrastructure, and the website is functional but outdated. There is a massive gap between who they are and how they show up online
Med spa content - before and afters, treatment walkthroughs, skin education - is one of the highest-performing categories on TikTok and Reels. A 30-year spa with a physician on staff and real clinical results has extraordinary content potential that is completely untapped
Dr. Nassif's credentials - fellowships in New York and Honolulu, recognized as one of America's Top Doctors since 2007 - are barely mentioned anywhere online. This is a powerful trust signal that should be front and center in all content and advertising
The Groupon history is a signal: at some point discounting became the acquisition strategy. That tells you client acquisition has been a persistent challenge. We replace discounting with a system that attracts full-price, high-value clients consistently
REVENUE LEAKS TO PROBE ON THIS CALL
With 30 years in business, ask how much of their revenue is coming from repeat clients vs. new clients. If it is heavily repeat-dependent, that is a retention strength but also a vulnerability - one bad season or a key staff departure could tank revenue overnight
Ask about their rebooking process. Are clients being rebooked at checkout, or are they leaving without a next appointment? This is one of the most common and costly revenue leaks in med spas
Ask about their retail attachment rate. They carry Integraderm, Revision SkinCare, and SkinCeuticals - premium product lines. If estheticians are not actively recommending and selling retail at every visit, they are leaving significant money on the table
The Integraderm proprietary line is an asset that is almost certainly underperforming. It is only available through the spa, which means there is no e-commerce, no recurring product revenue, and no way to monetize it beyond in-person visits. That is a fixable problem
Ask about gift card redemption rates and whether they track it. Gift cards are often sold and never redeemed - understanding that gap can reveal hidden revenue
SYSTEMS AND STAFF TO PROBE ON THIS CALL
Ask how they handle appointment reminders, cancellations, and no-shows. With a medical spa, no-shows are expensive. If they do not have an automated system managing this, it is costing them real money every week
Ask how new staff are onboarded and trained on the spa's standards and service philosophy. With a 30-year legacy, the culture Susan has built is valuable - but if it lives only in her head and not in a documented system, it is fragile
Ask how client consultations are structured. Are estheticians doing thorough intake consultations and building personalized treatment plans, or are clients just booking individual services? A proper consultation process dramatically increases average client spend and retention
Ask how they collect and use client feedback. With such strong loyalty, there is likely a wealth of testimonials and referral potential that is being left unactivated
THE BIG PICTURE
Susan is a skilled operator who has kept this business alive and respected for three decades. The goal of this call is not to tell her what is broken - it is to show her that the foundation she has built is strong enough to scale, and that we are the team to help her do it without it falling apart in the process
Fort Myers and Cape Coral are growing fast. Newer, well-funded med spas are entering the market with polished systems and digital strategies. IntegraLife has the credibility, the loyalty, and the clinical depth to dominate - but only if the business infrastructure catches up to the quality of the treatments

CONFIDENTIAL - THE LUXORA COLLECTIVE

Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation."
     4	license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
     5	---
     6	
     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `pandoc` or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	### Converting .doc to .docx
    22	
    23	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    24	
    25	```bash
    26	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    27	```
    28	
    29	### Reading Content
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	# Text extraction with tracked changes
    33	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    34	
    35	# Raw XML access
    36	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    37	```
    38	
    39	### Converting to Images
    40	
    41	```bash
    42	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    43	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    44	```
    45	
    46	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    47	
    48	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    49	
    50	```bash
    51	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    52	```
    53	
    54	---
    55	
    56	## Creating New Documents
    57	
    58	Generate .docx files with JavaScript, then validate. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    59	
    60	### Setup
    61	```javascript
    62	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    63	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    64	        InternalHyperlink, Bookmark, FootnoteReferenceRun, PositionalTab,
    65	        PositionalTabAlignment, PositionalTabRelativeTo, PositionalTabLeader,
    66	        TabStopType, TabStopPosition, Column, SectionType,
    67	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,
    68	        VerticalAlign, PageNumber, PageBreak } = require('docx');
    69	
    70	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    71	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    72	```
    73	
    74	### Validation
    75	After creating the file, validate it. If validation fails, unpack, fix the XML, and repack.
    76	```bash
    77	python scripts/office/validate.py doc.docx
    78	```
    79	
    80	### Page Size
    81	
    82	```javascript
    83	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    84	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    85	sections: [{
    86	  properties: {
    87	    page: {
    88	      size: {
    89	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    90	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    91	      },
    92	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
    93	    }
    94	  },
    95	  children: [/* content */]
    96	}]
    97	```
    98	
    99	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
   100	
   101	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
   102	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
   103	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
   104	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
   105	
   106	**Landscape orientation:** docx-js swaps width/height internally, so pass portrait dimensions and let it handle the swap:
   107	```javascript
   108	size: {
   109	  width: 12240,   // Pass SHORT edge as width
   110	  height: 15840,  // Pass LONG edge as height
   111	  orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE  // docx-js swaps them in the XML
   112	},
   113	// Content width = 15840 - left margin - right margin (uses the long edge)
   114	```
   115	
   116	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)
   117	
   118	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.
   119	
   120	```javascript
   121	const doc = new Document({
   122	  styles: {
   123	    default: { document: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 24 } } }, // 12pt default
   124	    paragraphStyles: [
   125	      // IMPORTANT: Use exact IDs to override built-in styles
   126	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   127	        run: { size: 32, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   128	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 240 }, outlineLevel: 0 } }, // outlineLevel required for TOC
   129	      { id: "Heading2", name: "Heading 2", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   130	        run: { size: 28, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   131	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 180, after: 180 }, outlineLevel: 1 } },
   132	    ]
   133	  },
   134	  sections: [{
   135	    children: [
   136	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   137	    ]
   138	  }]
   139	});
   140	```
   141	
   142	### Lists (NEVER use unicode bullets)
   143	
   144	```javascript
   145	// ❌ WRONG - never manually insert bullet characters
   146	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("• Item")] })  // BAD
   147	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("\u2022 Item")] })  // BAD
   148	
   149	// ✅ CORRECT - use numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET
   150	const doc = new Document({
   151	  numbering: {
   152	    config: [
   153	      { reference: "bullets",
   154	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.BULLET, text: "•", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   155	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   156	      { reference: "numbers",
   157	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.DECIMAL, text: "%1.", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   158	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   159	    ]
   160	  },
   161	  sections: [{
   162	    children: [
   163	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "bullets", level: 0 },
   164	        children: [new TextRun("Bullet item")] }),
   165	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "numbers", level: 0 },
   166	        children: [new TextRun("Numbered item")] }),
   167	    ]
   168	  }]
   169	});
   170	
   171	// ⚠️ Each reference creates INDEPENDENT numbering
   172	// Same reference = continues (1,2,3 then 4,5,6)
   173	// Different reference = restarts (1,2,3 then 1,2,3)
   174	```
   175	
   176	### Tables
   177	
   178	**CRITICAL: Tables need dual widths** - set both `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on each cell. Without both, tables render incorrectly on some platforms.
   179	
   180	```javascript
   181	// CRITICAL: Always set table width for consistent rendering
   182	// CRITICAL: Use ShadingType.CLEAR (not SOLID) to prevent black backgrounds
   183	const border = { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 1, color: "CCCCCC" };
   184	const borders = { top: border, bottom: border, left: border, right: border };
   185	
   186	new Table({
   187	  width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Always use DXA (percentages break in Google Docs)
   188	  columnWidths: [4680, 4680], // Must sum to table width (DXA: 1440 = 1 inch)
   189	  rows: [
   190	    new TableRow({
   191	      children: [
   192	        new TableCell({
   193	          borders,
   194	          width: { size: 4680, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Also set on each cell
   195	          shading: { fill: "D5E8F0", type: ShadingType.CLEAR }, // CLEAR not SOLID
   196	          margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }, // Cell padding (internal, not added to width)
   197	          children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("Cell")] })]
   198	        })
   199	      ]
   200	    })
   201	  ]
   202	})
   203	```
   204	
   205	**Table width calculation:**
   206	
   207	Always use `WidthType.DXA` — `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` breaks in Google Docs.
   208	
   209	```javascript
   210	// Table width = sum of columnWidths = content width
   211	// US Letter with 1" margins: 12240 - 2880 = 9360 DXA
   212	width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA },
   213	columnWidths: [7000, 2360]  // Must sum to table width
   214	```

   378	### Critical Rules for docx-js
   379	
   380	- **Set page size explicitly** - docx-js defaults to A4; use US Letter (12240 x 15840 DXA) for US documents
   381	- **Landscape: pass portrait dimensions** - docx-js swaps width/height internally; pass short edge as `width`, long edge as `height`, and set `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE`

   397	
   398	## Editing Existing Documents
   399	
   400	**Follow all 3 steps in order.**
   401	
   402	### Step 1: Unpack
   403	```bash
   404	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
   405	```
   406	Extracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`“` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.
   407	
   408	### Step 2: Edit XML
   409	
   410	Edit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.
   411	
   412	**Use "Claude" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.
   413	
   414	**Use the Edit tool directly for string replacement. Do not write Python scripts.** Scripts introduce unnecessary complexity. The Edit tool shows exactly what is being replaced.
   415	
   416	**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:
   417	```xml
   418	<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->
   419	<w:t>Here’s a quote: “Hello”</w:t>
   420	```
   421	| Entity | Character |
   422	|--------|-----------|
   423	| `‘` | ‘ (left single) |
   424	| `’` | ’ (right single / apostrophe) |
   425	| `“` | “ (left double) |
   426	| `”` | ” (right double) |
   427	
   428	**Adding comments:** Use `comment.py` to handle boilerplate across multiple XML files (text must be pre-escaped XML):
   429	```bash
   430	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Comment text with & and ’"
   431	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 "Reply text" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0
   432	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Text" --author "Custom Author"  # custom author name
   433	```

   435	
   436	### Step 3: Pack
   437	```bash
   438	python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
   439	```

   442	**Auto-repair will fix:**
   443	- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)
   444	- Missing `xml:space="preserve"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace

   446	**Auto-repair won't fix:**
   447	- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations
   448	
   449	### Common Pitfalls
   450	
   451	- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.
   452	- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.
   453	
   454	---
   455	
   456	## XML Reference

   458	### Schema Compliance

   460	- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last
   461	- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces
   462	- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)
   463	
   464	### Tracked Changes
